title: 2022 HMMT February Algebra and Number Theory Problem 3
statement: Let \(x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots, x_{2022}\) be nonzero real numbers. Suppose that \(x_{k}+\frac{1}{x_{k+1}}<0\) for each \(1 \leq k \leq 2022\), where \(x_{2023}=x_{1}\). Compute the maximum possible number of integers \(1 \leq n \leq 2022\) such that \(x_{n}>0\).

solutions.text:
Let the answer be \(M\). If \(M>1011\), there would exist two consecutive positive terms \(x_{k}, x_{k+1}\) which contradicts the assumption that \(x_{k}+\frac{1}{x_{k+1}}<0\). Thus, \(M \leq 1011\). If \(M=1011\), then the \(2022 x_{i}\) s must alternate between positive and negative. WLOG, assume \(x_{2 k-1}>0\) and \(x_{2 k}<0\) for each \(k\). Then, we have

\[\begin{aligned}
& x_{2 k-1}+\frac{1}{x_{2 k}}<0 \Longrightarrow\left|x_{2 k-1} x_{2 k}\right|<1, \\
& x_{2 k}+\frac{1}{x_{2 k+1}}<0 \Longrightarrow\left|x_{2 k} x_{2 k+1}\right|>1 .
\end{aligned}\]

Multiplying the first equation over all \(k\) gives us \(\prod_{i=1}^{2022}\left|x_{i}\right|<1\), while multiplying the second equation over all \(k\) gives us \(\prod_{i=1}^{2022}\left|x_{i}\right|>1\). Thus, we must have \(M<1011\).
\(M=1010\) is possible by the following construction:

\[1,-\frac{1}{2}, 3,-\frac{1}{4}, \ldots, 2019,-\frac{1}{2020},-10000,-10000\]
